analyst_view.overall: Leipzig (30th) and Lens (33rd) both have 3 points and need wins to stay in the race for the top 24. Lens are in turmoil: Pierre Sage left for Nice, and Didier Digard takes charge for the first time against Toulouse on 21 November, so this will be only his second game. Lens also lost 9-1 at home to Como in this competition. For Lens, striker Odsonne Édouard and Andrija Bulatović are out, and their away fans are banned by UEFA. Leipzig, 4th in the Bundesliga, get midfielder Neil El Aynaoui back from a calf injury. The numbers already count Lens's heavy recent conceding but know nothing about the coaching change. No referee has been named.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals and add about 6% to Leipzig for Lens's leaky recent defending. A new coach usually starts by organising the defence, and Lens will also be without striker Édouard, who isn't on the numbers' missing list. I go slightly lower, to about 3.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, split fairly evenly. Leipzig's lower recent corner count is already counted (-2%), and the coaching change at Lens says nothing clear about wide play. I stay at 10.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, with Leipzig's quieter recent disciplinary record counted (-9%). A team under a new coach and fighting for its season can play with more edge, but there is no hard news to size, and no referee is named. I stay at 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.4 shots and already trim Lens's side (-7%) for their low recent shot count. El Aynaoui's return helps Leipzig control the ball, and Édouard's absence takes some shots from Lens; these roughly cancel out. I stay at 27.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.2 shots on target and add about 12% to Leipzig for how often Lens have been opened up. If Digard tightens the shape and Édouard is missing up front, I expect a little less, so I go to about 10.9.
